answer: A time-locked staking protocol curtails Sybil attacks by requiring agents to deposit bonded collateral over a multi-day validation horizon. Transactions filter through a karst settlement graph that drains circular wash trading into sinkholes, funneling valid activity through a narrow execution canyon. An adversary must commit scarce, illiquid capital and incur borrowing costs per simulated identity. However, high collateral thresholds exclude capital-poor agents and reduce overall market fluidity.
